stories.body: Paraguay’s lower house voted 78–0 to impeach President Santiago Peña after he offered to resign following the collapse of Ueno Bank, which left millions of customers unable to access their accounts. A joint congressional session called to consider his resignation lost its quorum, and the Senate summoned him to an impeachment hearing. Lawmakers have questioned Peña’s former stake in Ueno’s parent company and whether officials concealed the lender’s problems. A conviction would deny him the lifetime Senate seat and associated legal immunity normally granted to former presidents.
stories.headline: Paraguay’s Congress rejects president’s resignation amid banking crisis

stories.body: Israel’s Arab-led Joint List said it would recommend opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form the next government, joining the Arab-led Ra’am party. Their support would give Eisenkot the expected backing of 67 lawmakers in the 120-seat Knesset, although he would still need to assemble a governing coalition. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc has 53 seats, but an ultra-Orthodox faction said it would recommend neither candidate after a dispute over military exemptions. President Isaac Herzog is consulting parties before choosing whom to task with forming a government.
stories.headline: Israel’s Arab Joint List backs Eisenkot to form a government

stories.body: Hoax bomb threats disrupted at least 34 flights across Europe this week, prompting diversions, emergency landings and aircraft searches. At least 25 flights were affected on Thursday alone, but all landed safely and searches found nothing suspicious. Investigators said there was no evidence so far that a hostile state or terrorist group was responsible. Some emails claimed to be from a Russian far-right movement, but its founder did not claim responsibility, and European authorities said it was too early to determine whether the incidents were linked.
stories.headline: Hoax bomb threats disrupt dozens of flights across Europe

stories.body: Teachers, hospital staff, rail workers and students joined a general strike and largely peaceful demonstrations across France against living costs, proposed public spending cuts and poor conditions in schools. The government estimated turnout at 600,000 or more, while the CGT union put it at nearly 1.6 million. The protests come as the government struggles to pass a tightening budget through a divided parliament and students continue to blockade schools over overcrowding and deteriorating buildings.
stories.headline: Hundreds of thousands protest across France over living costs

stories.body: Nearly 90 million forcibly displaced people, about three-quarters of the global total, live in countries highly exposed to climate hazards, the UN refugee agency said. It warned ahead of the COP31 climate summit in Turkey that droughts, floods and extreme heat are making lasting solutions for displaced people harder to find.
stories.headline: Three in four displaced people live in countries highly exposed to climate hazards, UN says

stories.body: Governor Gavin Newsom announced that he would commute the sentences of all 548 people on California’s death row to life without parole, citing moral concerns and the risk of error. The state has not carried out an execution in 20 years. About two-thirds of the commutations require California Supreme Court review because the prisoners have multiple felony convictions, according to the Death Penalty Information Center.
stories.headline: California governor announces plan to commute all 548 death sentences

stories.body: Technology and AI-related shares led a steep US market decline on Thursday, reversing gains made after the midterm election. Investors reassessed the outlook for data centers after voters backed restrictions in many local ballot measures and Democrats won races in states with major projects. At midday, the Nasdaq was down 4.8%, Nvidia had fallen about 8% and several data center companies had dropped more sharply. UBS analysts estimated that construction pauses could put roughly 30% of planned US data center capacity additions in 2028 at risk.
stories.headline: AI stocks fall as investors weigh election results and data center restrictions

stories.body: Bernie Sanders and progressive campaigners argue that Democratic wins in states including Texas and Michigan show the strength of a message focused on living standards, inequality and the influence of wealthy donors. Sanders cited candidates who echoed themes he has promoted for years, while strategist Morris Katz argued that clear economic messaging helped them withstand attacks on cultural issues. Their interpretation is a claim about why candidates won, and the election has also renewed debate over the party’s direction and its 2028 presidential field.
stories.headline: Progressives point to economic populism after Democratic midterm victories

stories.body: Michigan senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed won statewide but ran well behind governor-elect Jocelyn Benson in heavily Jewish communities, according to a Politico analysis of precinct results. In Huntington Woods, he received 65.3% to Benson’s 80%, compared with a two-point gap statewide. El-Sayed faced criticism from some Jewish Democrats over his position on Israel and remarks after a synagogue attack, for which he later apologized. He said he would not change his position on Israel but hoped to earn support by working on shared concerns and serving all constituents.
stories.headline: Abdul El-Sayed ran behind other Michigan Democrats in heavily Jewish communities

stories.body: Rail infrastructure manager Adif acknowledged in a 2019 contract that its system for communications between traffic controllers and trains was susceptible to errors or manipulation. The contract began a project to digitize the system and reduce the likelihood and effects of human error, but the project remains in progress and has not been deployed across the network. Separately, El País reported that the Iryo train involved in the Urda collision had undergone an extensive inspection two days before the crash.
stories.headline: Adif identified risk of human error in train communications years before Urda crash

stories.body: Civil Guard investigators searched former transport minister José Luis Ábalos’s home in Valencia as part of a new branch of the Koldo investigation into alleged irregularities during his time in office. Six people were detained and later released, according to El Periódico, and investigators also requested documents from rail infrastructure agency Adif. The suspected offenses include influence peddling, criminal organization and money laundering. Ábalos is already in prison after a conviction over irregularities in pandemic mask purchases.
stories.headline: Police search former minister Ábalos’s home in new Koldo investigation

stories.body: Koldo García, the jailed former adviser to José Luis Ábalos, alleged in recordings sent to Cadena SER that a People’s Party lawyer offered to cover his defense costs and pay him €1 million for information that could bring down Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez. García also alleged he was asked to provide information even if it was false; PP sources called the accusations false. His lawyer has submitted invoices showing that the publisher of OKDiario paid €242,000 toward his defense, but those invoices do not establish the alleged wider deal.
stories.headline: Koldo García alleges PP lawyer offered him money for information against Sánchez

stories.body: The Ibero-American summit in Madrid adopted a joint declaration and agreed to meet again in Honduras in 2028, after its previous gathering failed to produce a common statement. Heads of state or government from 10 of the 22 countries attended, with the others represented by senior officials. Argentina, Colombia, Costa Rica and Paraguay dissociated themselves from one clause opposing coercive measures contrary to international law that hinder countries’ development priorities.
stories.headline: Ibero-American summit agrees joint declaration despite many leaders’ absence

stories.body: During the 24-hour general strike on Wednesday, November 11, Rodalies, FGC, metro, tram and urban and interurban buses must provide 25% of their usual service during peak periods, from 6:30 to 9:30 a.m. and 4:30 to 9 p.m. The Barcelona airport bus must run at 50% throughout the day. Emergency medical services and specialist units will operate normally, while minimum staffing rules also apply to primary care, schools and emergency services.
stories.headline: Catalunya sets minimum public transport service for November 11 general strike

stories.body: Barcelona’s city council approved a proposal calling for stronger enforcement of national restrictions on certain purchases by large property holders and real estate companies. It also asks the city government to begin planning changes that would allow Barcelona to apply a proposed Catalan ban on speculative purchases once regional legislation is approved. The proposal calls for quarterly reports on enforcement; it does not itself establish the future ban.
stories.headline: Barcelona advances plan to curb speculative home purchases

stories.body: Barcelona’s council gave initial approval to a city and Generalitat company intended to rehabilitate 4,000 homes in Besòs-Maresme by 2038, under a €415 million plan. The first phase provides for €95 million through 2029. Residents and some council members have raised concerns about possible demolitions after a technical report examined a scenario involving 1,800 homes; deputy mayor Laia Bonet said considering that scenario did not mean it had been chosen.
stories.headline: Barcelona approves public company to rehabilitate homes in Besòs-Maresme

stories.body: Barcelona will require proof of city residency for its next two rounds of €20 culture vouchers after the first 20,000 were claimed in less than a day. The city said about 20% of the first round went to applicants from elsewhere in Catalunya, prompting criticism from ERC. The next application rounds are scheduled to begin January 11 and April 26. Vouchers can be used for live performances, Catalan-language cinema and books.
stories.headline: Barcelona will restrict future culture vouchers to city residents
